method.boundary: LINUX CPU PROXY ONLY. These are movement-complete→result-interactive PROXY latencies for the analyze pipeline run with --reuse-extract (pose/people/ball/extract metadata pre-generated and held constant); they are NEVER device (iPhone/Mac/Apple Vision) numbers and no device claim is made or implied. No accuracy/cascade claims are derived from these runs. Frames are never counted as independent trials; every distribution below is grouped per clip and pooled across the two committed dev clips.

latencyVsTargets.verdictOnThisProxy: Warm P50 16.2s and cold P50 47.9s both exceed the 5s max target by >3x on this Linux CPU proxy. No RC regression vs the same-machine pre-integration baseline (warm pooled P50 improved 20.3s -> 16.2s; cold improved 61.7s -> 47.9s); absolute numbers are dominated by CPU-only D-FINE paddle detection and are NOT device numbers. Whether the shipping device meets <=5s cannot be measured here (no iPhone/Mac available).

p1.title: Serve-mode paddle worker loses queued requests under concurrency: ffmpeg inherits the worker's stdin and swallows JSONL request lines
p1.rootCause: detect_paddle.py spawned ffmpeg via subprocess.Popen(stdout=PIPE) without detaching stdin. ffmpeg reads its inherited stdin for interactive key commands, so any request line queued on the worker's stdin while a decode is running can be consumed by ffmpeg instead of the serve loop. That request never gets a response, times out after requestTimeoutMs (default 30min), the client kills the worker, and every queued/subsequent request in the session fails. Sequential use never has queued bytes during a decode, which is why the e18 sequential soak (200/200) never caught it.
p1.impact: Session instability under concurrent/queued analysis (Try Again spam, multi-event sessions): observed 19/40 then 7/60 request survival with a 30-minute stall before total worker loss.
p1.fix: stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL on both ffmpeg Popen sites in tools/paddle-lab/detect_paddle.py
p1.regressionTest: packages/swing-lab/test/paddleWorker.test.ts — 'every subprocess.Popen in detect_paddle.py detaches stdin' (source contract), plus post-fix soak evidence 40/40 and repro 60/60
p1.verification: pre-fix repro 7/60 ok -> post-fix 60/60 ok; full soak real-concurrent 19/40 -> 40/40

p1.title: Movement-complete→result-interactive proxy latency far exceeds targets on Linux CPU (warm P50 16.2s vs <=5s max)
p1.detail: On this Linux CPU-only proxy the pipeline cannot meet the 2/3/5s bands; paddle detection (D-FINE on CPU) is >90% of wall. This matches the recorded Wave E e17 profile (warm P50 ~15.6s same machine class) — it is a known CPU-proxy property, NOT a new RC regression (RC is faster than the pre-integration baseline on the same machine: warm pooled P50 20.3s -> 16.2s). Whether shipping devices (iPhone ANE / Apple Vision path) meet the targets is unmeasurable here; no honest Linux fix exists because the dominant cost is the detector model on CPU.
p1.disposition: Cannot be closed internally: requires on-device measurement (external hardware). Recorded as unresolved rather than softened.

p2.title: Cold start adds ~30s+ over warm on Linux (page-cache-dropped P50 47.9s vs warm 16.2s), dominated by python import + torch/model load and cold file reads
p2.note: device cold start will differ; recorded for completeness

verdictRationale: Honest gate reading: the mandatory latency targets (<=5s max) are not met on the only platform we can measure (Linux CPU proxy: warm P50 16.2s, P95 55.2s, n=16 pooled over 2 clips; cold P50 47.9s, n=6). There is NO RC regression versus the same-machine pre-integration baseline (RC is faster cold and warm), no degrading Try Again latency (negative slopes over 12 attempts/clip), no unbounded memory growth (bounded max RSS; negative worker RSS slope over 100 requests), scheduling stays correct under sustained 120-stroke backlog, and worker restart works. One P1 Session-stability release blocker (concurrent request loss via ffmpeg stdin inheritance) was found, root-caused, fixed, and regression-tested. The gate cannot honestly be marked PASS on measured evidence, and it is not purely BLOCKED_EXTERNAL because the Linux measurement itself is valid and fails the stated bands; device-side adjudication (iPhone/Mac) remains externally blocked and could overturn the latency finding but no such evidence exists.
honesty: No device numbers claimed or implied. Held-out cases untouched. No thresholds, denominators, or assertions weakened; the pre-fix failing soak artifact is committed alongside the post-fix one. Wave G g23 artifacts do not exist on the remote and are disclosed as missing rather than substituted.
